source_text: δεῖν μητέρα τοῖς τέκνοις ἐν ἡμέρᾳ μιᾷ, τί ἂν εἴη πάλιν; {ΚΥΡ.} Νομοθετήσας εὖ μάλα τὰ ἐπὶ Χριστῷ, καὶ τὴν δι' αὐτοῦ τελείωσιν προαναφωνήσας ἀστείως, οὐκ ἠγνόησεν, ὡς Θεὸς, τῶν Ἰουδαίων τὸ ἀπειθὲς, καὶ τῆς Ἱερουσαλὴμ τὸ δυσήνιον, καὶ ὅτι ταύτης ἕνεκα τῆς αἰτίας, ὀλοθρευθήσονται μὲν ὡς κυριοκτόνοι, καὶ ἀγρίως πεπαρῳνηκότες εἰς τὸν Υἱὸν οἱ ἐξ Ἰσραὴλ, πλὴν οὐκ εἰσάπαν ὁλόριζος Ἱερουσαλὴμ οἰχήσεται, μενεῖ δὲ ὥσπερ ἔρημος τέκνων, τὸν τελευταῖον καὶ ἐν ἐσχάτοις περιμένουσα καιρὸν, καθ' ὃν καὶ αὐτὴ σωθήσεται κατόπιν τρέχουσα τῶν ἐθνῶν· τέθειται γὰρ εἰς νῶτον, τοῦτ' ἔστιν, ὀπίσω, κατὰ τὴν τοῦ Ψάλλοντος φωνὴν, «Ὅτι θήσει αὐτοὺς νῶτον·» πᾶς γὰρ Ἰσραὴλ σωθήσεται, τῆς ἐξ ἐθνῶν ἀγέλης τοῖς θείοις σηκοῖς προενηυλισμένης. Οὐκ ἐᾷ τοιγαροῦν ὁ νόμος τὴν ὡς ἐν ἐσχάτῃ πανωλεθρίᾳ γενέσθαι φθορὰν, ἡμερότητι συγκεκραμένην τὴν ἐπὶ τοῖς ἀπειθήσασι προαναφαίνων ὀργὴν, ἐν ταὐτῷ δὲ, οἶμαι τύπων ὥσπερ τινὰ τὸ χρῆμα τιθεὶς εἰδήσεως ἀναγκαίας. Ἥκιστα μὲν γὰρ οἰχήσεται τὰ ὄντα πρὸς τὸ μηδὲν ἀκράτῳ φθορᾷ τυραννούμενα, διαμενεῖ δὲ ὥσπερ ταῖς διαδοχαῖς τοῦτο ἐν ἐκείνῳ, κἀκεῖνο τυχὸν ἐν τούτῳ σωζόμενα, κατά γε τὸ συγγενὲς ἢ ὁμοειδὲς, τὸν εἰσάπαν ὄλεθρον τῶν ἰδίων κτισμάτων ἀποσοβοῦντος τοῦ Θεοῦ. «Ἔκτισε γὰρ εἰς τὸ εἶναι τὰ πάντα καὶ σωτήριοι αἱ γενέσεις τοῦ κόσμου,» κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον. Ἔπρεπε δὲ καὶ τῶν τοιούτων ἡ προαγόρευσις, καὶ μὴν καὶ ἡ δήλωσις, τῶν περὶ Χριστοῦ λόγων, δι' ὃν καὶ ἐν ᾧ τὰ ἐφθαρμένα σώζεται, καὶ τὸ θανάτῳ τυραννούμενον ἀνατέθηλεν εἰς ζωὴν, τετελεύτηκε μὲν γὰρ ἡ ῥίζα τοῦ ἀνθρωπείου γένους οἷά τις μήτηρ, ὡς ἐν Ἀδὰμ, πλὴν οἱ ἐξ αὐτῆς, τοῦτ' ἔστιν, ἡμεῖς, ἀνεθάλλομεν ἐν Χριστῷ καὶ ἐσμὲν καὶ σωζόμεθα, ζωὴν ἔχοντες αὐτὸν καὶ ῥίζαν ὥσπερ τοῦ γένους δευτέραν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ὡς εὖ γε δὴ καὶ μάλα ἀπεζεσμένως ὁ λόγος ἔχει. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἄξιον δὲ, ὦ Παλλάδιε, τοῖς εἰρημένοις ἐπενεγκεῖν, τό· «Οὐ φυτεύσεις σεαυτῷ ἄλσος· πᾶν ξύλον παρὰ τὸ θυσιαστήριον Κυρίου τοῦ Θεοῦ σου, οὐ ποιήσεις σεαυτῷ, οὐ στήσεις σεαυτῷ στήλην, ἃ ἐμίσησε Κύριος ὁ Θεός σου.» Θέα γὰρ ὅπως εἰδωλοπρεποῦς ἀπάτης ἐξοικίζει παντελῶς τὸν τῆς ἀληθείας προσκυνητὴν, ἥκιστα μὲν ἐφιεὶς, τοῖς Ἑλλήνων ἀποκεχρῆσθαι νόμοις, ἀποσείεσθαι δὲ δεῖν τὰ παρ' ἐκείνοις ἔθη παρεγγυῶν, κἂν εἰ μηδὲν ἔχοιεν τὸ λυποῦν, καὶ εἰ γένοιντο τυχόν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Οἷόν τι φής; {ΚΥΡ.} Τὰ εὐερνέστατα τῶν φυτῶν πάντα τε ἀμφιλαφῶς κομῶντα δρυμὸν καταλαμβάνοντες Ἕλληνες. βωμοὺς καὶ θυσίας τοῖς δαιμονίοις ἵστασαν. Ἔδει γὰρ, ἔδει τοῖς τῶν δαιμονίων βωμοῖς ἀποφορὰν ὥσπερ νοῦ, καὶ μὴν καὶ τέρψεις παραπεπῆχθαι κοσμικάς. Νοσεῖ γὰρ τὸ ψεῦδος οἴκοθεν μὲν τὸ ἄναλκι, κατακαλλύνεται δὲ πολλάκις τοῖς εἰσποιητοῖς ὡραϊσμοῖς,
pass_a_gloss: Palladius: ...[that the mother must not be destroyed together] with the children (τέκνα) on one day, what would it be again? Cyril: Having legislated (νομοθετέω) very well the things concerning Christ, and having foretold (προαναφωνέω) elegantly (ἀστείως) the perfecting (τελείωσις) through him, he was not ignorant, as God, of the disobedience (τὸ ἀπειθές) of the Jews and the unruliness (τὸ δυσήνιον) of Jerusalem, and that for this cause those from Israel would be destroyed (ὀλοθρεύω) as Lord-killers (κυριοκτόνοι), having savagely behaved drunkenly/outrageously (παροινέω) toward the Son; yet Jerusalem will not entirely perish root-and-all (ὁλόριζος), but will remain as bereft (ἔρημος) of children, awaiting the last time in the end (ἐν ἐσχάτοις), at which she too will be saved running behind (κατόπιν) the nations (ἔθνη). For she has been set at the back (νῶτον), that is, behind, according to the voice of the Psalmist: For he will set them [as] back. For all Israel will be saved, the flock (ἀγέλη) from the nations having first been folded (προαυλίζομαι) in the divine pens (σηκοί). So the law does not permit the destruction (φθορά) to happen as in final utter ruin (πανωλεθρία), showing beforehand the wrath (ὀργή) upon the disobedient as mixed with gentleness (ἡμερότης); at the same time, I think, setting the matter as a kind of type(s) of necessary knowledge (εἴδησις ἀναγκαία). For existing things will by no means go to nothing, tyrannized by unmixed (ἄκρατος) corruption, but will endure as by successions (διαδοχαί), this in that and that perhaps in this being preserved, according to the kindred (συγγενές) or same-in-kind (ὁμοειδές), God warding off (ἀποσοβέω) total ruin of his own creatures (κτίσματα). For he created (κτίζω) all things for being, and saving (σωτήριοι) the generations (γενέσεις) of the world, as written. Fitting (πρέπω) was the foretelling (προαγόρευσις) of such things, and also the disclosure (δήλωσις), of the words about Christ, through whom and in whom the corrupted are saved, and the death-tyrannized has blossomed again (ἀναθάλλω) into life; for the root (ῥίζα) of the human race died like a mother, as in Adam, but those from it, we, blossomed again in Christ and are and are saved, having him as life and as a second root of the race. Palladius: How well and very carefully (ἀπεζεσμένως) the account holds. Cyril: Worthy, Palladius, to add to what was said: You shall not plant for yourself a grove (ἄλσος); every tree (ξύλον) beside the altar (θυσιαστήριον) of the Lord your God you shall not make for yourself; you shall not set up for yourself a pillar (στήλη), which the Lord your God hated. See how he removes (ἐξοικίζω) entirely from idol-befitting (εἰδωλοπρεπής) deceit (ἀπάτη) the worshipper (προσκυνητής) of the truth, by no means permitting to use the laws of the Greeks (Ἕλληνες), enjoining (παρεγγυάω) to shake off (ἀποσείω) their customs (ἔθη), even if they had nothing harmful (τὸ λυποῦν) and if they should happen by chance. Palladius: Such as what do you say? Cyril: The best-grown (εὐερνέστατα) of plants and all luxuriantly leafy (ἀμφιλαφῶς κομῶντα) thicket (δρυμός) seizing, Greeks set up altars and sacrifices to the demons (δαιμόνια). For it was needed, needed, to the demons' altars a carrying-away (ἀποφορά) as of mind, and also worldly delights (τέρψεις κοσμικαί), to be fixed beside. For falsehood (ψεῦδος) is sick from within with feebleness (τὸ ἄναλκι), but is often beautified (κατακαλλύνω) with adopted/imported (εἰσποιητός) adornments (ὡραϊσμοί), [continues in section 29].
pass_b_english: Palladius: …together with her young on the same day: what, in turn, would that mean?

Cyril: After laying down in the law so well what concerns Christ, and gracefully foretelling the perfecting that comes through him, the Lawgiver, being God, did not fail to know the disobedience of the Jews and the unruliness of Jerusalem. He knew that for this reason the people of Israel would be destroyed as killers of the Lord and as men who had savagely abused the Son; yet Jerusalem would not perish altogether, root and all. She would remain like a woman bereft of children, waiting for the last time, at the end, when she too will be saved, running behind the nations. For she has been set at the back, that is, behind, as the Psalmist’s words have it: ‘For he will put them at the back’ (Psalm 21:12). For all Israel will be saved, once the flock from the nations has first been gathered into the divine folds (Romans 11:25–26). So the law does not allow the destruction to come about as a final and total ruin. It shows in advance that the wrath against the disobedient is tempered with gentleness; and at the same time, I think, it sets the matter before us as a kind of figure of something we need to know. For the things that exist will by no means pass away into nothing, overpowered by unchecked corruption. Rather, they will endure, as it were, through succession, this one preserved in that, and that perhaps in this, according to kinship or likeness of kind, since God wards off the total destruction of his own creatures. For ‘he created all things that they might exist, and the generations of the world bring preservation’ (Wisdom of Solomon 1:14), as it is written. And it was fitting that the foretelling of such things, and indeed their disclosure, should belong to the teaching about Christ, for whose sake and in whom what was corrupted is saved, and what was under the tyranny of death has blossomed again into life. For the root of the human race died like a mother, as in Adam (1 Corinthians 15:22); yet those who came from it, that is, we ourselves, have blossomed again in Christ. In him we exist and are saved, since we have him as our life and as a second root, so to speak, of our race.
Palladius: How well, and how carefully, your argument is worked out!

Cyril: It is worth adding to what has been said, Palladius, this passage: ‘You shall not plant a grove for yourself; any tree beside the altar of the Lord your God you shall not make for yourself; you shall not set up a pillar for yourself, things which the Lord your God hates’ (Deuteronomy 16:21–22). See how he removes the worshipper of the truth entirely from idolatrous deceit. He by no means allows him to make use of the laws of the pagans, and he charges him to shake off their customs, even if they do no harm and even if they come about by chance.

Cyril: The pagans would take over the most flourishing trees and every thicket dense with leaves, and there they would set up altars and sacrifices to the demons. For they had to, they simply had to, attach to the altars of the demons something that would carry the mind away, as it were, and worldly pleasures besides. Falsehood is sick with weakness from within, but it is often decked out with ornaments brought in from outside,

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril, De adoratione Book 10. Translated afresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the withheld earlier English was not used.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opening line completes Palladius' question begun at the end of section 27 (Leviticus 22:28). Psalm 21:12 is English numbering; LXX Psalm 20:13 reads ὅτι θήσεις αὐτοὺς νῶτον ('you will make them turn their back'); Cyril's text has third person θήσει and he reads νῶτον as 'behind', so rendered 'he will put them at the back' to keep his argument. 'All Israel will be saved' quotes Romans 11:26; the flock from the nations entering first alludes to Romans 11:25, hence 11:25–26. Wisdom of Solomon 1:14: σωτήριοι means 'wholesome' or 'bringing preservation'; rendered 'bring preservation' because Cyril's argument (kinds preserved through succession) rests on that sense. 'As in Adam' taken as a clear allusion to 1 Corinthians 15:22. The subject of 'having legislated' is not named in the Greek; 'the Lawgiver, being God' supplies it from ὡς Θεός. τύπων ὥσπερ τινὰ ... εἰδήσεως ἀναγκαίας is awkward (τύπων may be a misprint for τύπον); rendered 'a kind of figure of something we need to know'. ἀπεζεσμένως taken in Cyril's usual sense 'carefully, with refinement'. Ἕλληνες rendered 'the pagans' (Cyril means pagan worshippers, not Greeks as a nation). Deuteronomy 16:21: Cyril's text reads οὐ ποιήσεις σεαυτῷ where the common LXX text has ὃ ποιήσεις σεαυτῷ ('the altar ... which you will make for yourself'); followed Cyril. The section ends mid-sentence; it continues in section 29. δι' ὃν (accusative) rendered 'for whose sake', not 'through whom'.
